A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Banach Space|Banach space]] and $T$ a [[Definition:Bounded Linear Operator|bounded linear operator]] on $X$ with $
orm T < 1$.
Then $I - T$ is [[Definition:Invertible Bounded Linear Operator|invertible]], with:
:$\displaystyle \paren {I - T}^{-1} = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty T^n, \quad 
orm {\paren {I - T}^{-1} } \le  rac 1 {1 - 
orm T}$

B_source.statement:
Let $r \in \R$ with $\size r < 1$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty r^n = \frac 1 {1 - r}$

object_map.reformulation: Replace the scalar ratio by an operator and the absolute value by the operator norm; the telescoping identity survives since all terms are powers of T.

validity_conditions: The space of bounded operators must be complete, which holds as X is a Banach space.
Commutativity is used only among powers of T, so non-commutativity of operators causes no problem.
proof_plan:
By [[Definition:Submultiplicative Norm|submultiplicativity]], $
orm {T^n} \le 
orm T^n$.
As $\displaystyle \sum 
orm T^n$ converges, $\displaystyle \sum T^n$ converges absolutely in the Banach space of bounded operators, to some $S$.

Let $S_N = \displaystyle \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^N T^n$.
Then:
:$\paren {I - T} S_N = S_N \paren {I - T} = I - T^{N + 1}$
As $\norm {T^{N + 1} } \to 0$, letting $N \to \infty$ gives $\paren {I - T} S = S \paren {I - T} = I$.

Summing norms gives $
orm S \le \displaystyle \sum 
orm T^n =  rac 1 {1 - 
orm T}$.
This is the [[Neumann Series Theorem]].
{{qed}}
